en: I saw Śrī, I saw the golden body, I saw all of
the adorning colour of the shining sun, I saw
the golden disk that emerges in battles, I saw the spiralling conch in the hand
[all] on my [lord] with the colour of the ocean today
Today I saw the anklets [on his feet]; all seven births I cut off
You, Tirumāl, who saw [and] took up Śrī that day
into the blooming tulsi on [your] mountain chest bathed in gold
I saw [and] took [you] into [my] mind
He is in [my] mind; he is on the water of the great sea; he belongs
to her of the blossom; he with cool tulsi on [his] chest, he the colour
of the rising flood who rejoices in subduing the enemies so that they fall
in [their] anger, [he is] the remedy that ends coming hells
gloss: participial noun, imperfective aspect, honorific, third person

en: Remedy, wealth and ambrosia is he
Māl with perfect red eyes; there he stood in agreement
[with Bali], having swallowed [and] spit out the world, accepting water
[and] with three steps of [his] feet he spread over the world that day
gloss: participial noun, masculine singular, perfective aspect

en: The feet of him who that day spread over the world are the colour of lotuses
the colour of [his] body is the colour of the vast ocean’s water, the colour of [his]
crown is the light of the hot one with a single wheel. That, isn’t it
is the beauty of him who has the precious discus
gloss: participial noun, masculine singular, perfective aspect
participial noun, masculine singular, dative, perfective aspect

en: Isn’t it beautiful, the sea-water colour of him with the discus?
Isn’t it beautiful, the surpassing of the [cosmic] egg? Isn’t it beautiful
the ankleted [foot] of him who accepted water in [his] palm, [the foot] from which
flowed Ganges water when the one on the [lotus] blossom washed [his] feet
gloss: participial noun, masculine singular, dative, perfective aspect

en: We will worship the ankleted [feet] come, heart, to him who is difficult to fathom
thus measuring the beauty of the lord with the bird vehicle who measured
the garden [surrounded] by the water waves of the cloud[-coloured] sea
him who is far from any matter, him who is difficult to approach for us
Speaking many names, saying ‘Nārāyaṇa’
we will worship [him] with palms [joined], good heart come, together
let us see with our eyes Kaṇṇaṉ, with cool tulsi where bees hum
who ate [and] spat out the earthen world
The eyes lotuses, and just lotuses, the palms of [his] hands
and [his] feet that measured the earth again are such. Immeasurable
light [is] he, the colour of big black clouds, he the colour of the rain ocean’s water
he the colour of brilliant dark sapphire
Speaking of light, power, wealth and beauty
birth in a flawless family and other things
when one recites the names of him who held the right-spiralling pure conch
those will do good, go [and] well reach [him]
gloss: participial noun, singular, masculine, perfective aspect

en: He is the four Vedas that are well recited, the one of the colour of the torrent
of the foaming, flooding waterfall in which honey drips, the one of the milk
ocean with conches [and] waves, the one on the snake bed, the one of the sea of
treatises by those of well-trained discourse, the one of subtle knowledge
gloss: pronominalised noun, singular, masculine, third person
pronominalised noun, singular, masculine, third person
participial noun, imperfective aspect, honorific, third person
pronominalised noun, singular, masculine, third person

en: Those who perceive [him] well, well reciting what is called Veda, putting the bolt
called knowledge [and] closing the firm door called restraining
all five senses in themselves, they will see every day
the form of him with the colour of the fresh flood
gloss: participial noun, imperfective aspect, honorific, third person

en: While once in a circle he measured with [his] foot the lotus that is
the circle of the earth, receiving the world with water, the tall circle
of [his] crown cut into the middle of space [and] extended
up to the [top of the world] egg, [the crown] of Māl who stood as a great body
gloss: neuter singular, perfective aspect, verbal noun

en: When one curls the mind around Māl, letting go of women’s shoulders
keeping the mind on treatises becomes easy humbling oneself
before the feet of him whose feet are touched by the crowns of celestials
of him on Vēṅkatam, him who is the Vedas in four parts
The Lord, who rests on the bed of Aṉantaṉ
as if adorned with sapphires on [its] lowered hoods
while the constant waves of the ocean, which lowers [and] rises, dash
comes [and] rests on the bed of the mind of me, [his] servant
The red corals [and] the white pearls from the white waves
that come [and] crash become decorative lamps that illuminate the dusk
going to him of Tiruvallikēṇi, our father, the one with an excellent chest
that is one with her of the lotus, the unique creeper
Of the days gone by, any day is a day that was not gone by
[before I] said: ‘the red-eyed Māl is our Māl’
Let my mouth praise, without forgetting, being the servant
to both the feet of our Father who will never die
O tall Māl, you who speaking truth as a dwarf, measured
[and] took the earth from Māvali with three steps
bless [me] with being without fear as a servant
through all seven births to your undiminishing two feet that leapt [over the worlds]
Will he remain without being gracious, he who that day joined
the banyan leaf as an innocent child, to those who stand before [him]
as the foremost, [folding their] hands in worship [and] strewing red blossoms
for [his] red feet, being without darkness in [their] minds?
gloss: participial noun, singular, masculine, perfective aspect
participial noun, dative, imperfective aspect, honorific, third person

en: To you who first ate the world and spit [it] out, after [that] is measuring
that world with two steps [and] taking it something great? What
Tirumāl, tall one with red eyes, our
great lord, you tell [us] this
gloss: participial noun, dative, perfective aspect, singular, second person

en: To the extent that they talk, they will talk
about the form of him who killed Vakkaraṉ with a rising howl
the one with a garland of tulsi in fragrant blossoms, the one with the
fiery discus, the one with the conch, the one with the [bow], Śārṅga
gloss: participial noun, masculine singular, perfective aspect

en: Him with the form that is daily seen by celestials, bowing [their]
shapely crowns [and] strewing blossoms full of fragrance
directly melting inside, o heart
desire straightaway to see [him] truly
[My] mind, being stirred up into confusion, comes
to the [feet with] golden anklets of him with a tulsi garland from the fields
that bud for bees to go into [the flower] tubes [and] fill themselves up
while others with pretty wings that measured heaven [and] earth hum desirously
The one who, at the time he came, was vast land and dark sky, wind
and the form of approaching fire [and] water, the one who possesses
a singular befitting glowing discus, to the anklet that encirles his [feet]
link yourself daily, immerse yourself, heart, in worship
Is it a mistake, heart, if you worship exultantly
the one who is distant even for the celestials, the one who destroyed seven huge bulls
the one with a mouth that ate the butter of the cowherdess, her with dense curls
after eating the whole of the world [surrounded] by clear water?
gloss: participial noun, masculine singular, accusative, perfective aspect

en: He dwells also in my exultant mind, in the red-eyed
snake and in large Kacci with full excellence
the one with the cool tulsi who does not go beyond
Vēṅkaṭam, Veḵkā and the city of Vēḷukkai
gloss: neuter singular, perfective aspect, verbal noun

en: Who are those who have borne misery, where are those who have experienced sorrow
after daily approaching the one who takes
rest on the water bed, the cause, the one who directly
churned the black sea abounding in clouds?
gloss: participial noun, perfective aspect, honorific, third person
participial noun, perfective aspect, honorific, third person
participial noun, masculine singular, accusative, perfective aspect
participial noun, masculine singular, accusative, perfective aspect

en: He settled on the serpent bed, being of the Five [Pāṇḍavas] that day
he was mingled in the hot Bhārata war, and he was dejected
because of the churning stick in [the hand of] the cowherdess, o mother
the lord who had drunk the milk of the demoness with sharp teeth
gloss: neuter singular, perfective aspect, verbal noun
neuter singular, perfective aspect, verbal noun
neuter singular, perfective aspect, verbal noun

en: Again taking up the great lord who had drunk the milk of the demoness
the cowherdess fearlessly gave [him her] breast
joining with the one with words that were babbled, a sweet coral-red mouth
[and] a shining body full of lush darkness
gloss: participial noun, feminine singular, perfective aspect

en: The vast ocean with Śrī joined to [him], Kuṭantai, Vēṅkaṭam
my mind that consented, the full sky, the excellent Veda
Pāṭakam, Aṉantaṉ [it is] these that are the abodes
of the lord with the lush tulsi chaplet
These are temples of him the one who became the lion form
performing a pounding of Hiraṇya’s chest, the one on the snake
that does not perceive with the ears, the one in the four Vedas, the one with
him who receives the [Gaṅgā’s] nectar as part, the one on the milk ocean
gloss: participial noun, perfective aspect, singular, masculine
participial noun, perfective aspect, singular, masculine, third person

en: The milk ocean, Vēṅkaṭam, the snake, the dewy sky
the ocean of treatises and the heart of the one who sits arranged on the
lotus with fine fibres, [these] he took as [his] places
the cowherd who broke the wild lime tree
gloss: participial noun, perfective aspect, honorific, third person
participial noun, singular, masculine, perfective aspect

en: O you who, as a boy on a banyan leaf, gently ate
all the worlds on a former day, truly, infatuating one
that day you churned the sea of dark waters with the Mandara mountain
[and] gave the heavenly ambrosia to them of the intermediate space
gloss: participial noun, masculine singular, perfective aspect
participial noun, masculine singular, imperfective aspect
pronominalised noun, dative, honorific, third person

en: [Was there] weariness when he measured this world that day?
Look, heart, at the one who once overcame
Kaṃsa, the one of imperishable glory, the one who that day
stood, sat [and] lay in the large city of Vēḷukkai
gloss: participial noun, singular, masculine, accusative, third person
participial noun, masculine singular, accusative, perfective aspect

en: ‘Look, look,’ thus desire the eyes: the golden body of him
whose chest has ornaments shining with rays [and] garlands
The red-golden anklet of him with the pendant, around which bees hum
busily singing melodies, we will sing [and] worship, hands [folded]
In [his] hands the fiery discus, the white conch from the cloud[-coloured] sea
the cruel club, the Śārṅga bow, the hotly glowing sword
weapons red [from blood are] the Dark one’s who with [his] foot measured
the world [surrounded] by the chilly water, the surface [of the ocean his] place
In servitude to him I fell: he who is inside, who is outside
he who is in the water of the salty black sea, the very one on whose
holy chest glitters an ornamented necklace with many jewels
and the Lady of the flower with a mouth [like] red coral
He’s comparable only to himself. His form is every form
He is the form of penance, the stars is he
the lord who is the flaming fire, the great mountains, the eight directions
and the two lights of the [cosmic] egg
As lord, as the land, as the eight directions is he
as the Veda, the Veda’s meaning, as the sky is he
inside [my] heart, the one from Vēṅkaṭam with roaring water
shining with waterfalls of a white superior to the crescent moon
He is, look, good heart. Ever the highest
is he, look. In the hearts of those who think [of him] is he, see
the one from Vēṅkaṭam with swelling waterfalls where peaks are so high
as to hide the sky, the king who secretly measured the earth
gloss: participial noun, imperfective aspect, honorific, third person

en: He who, extending [his] crown with lasting gems, going to the [tip of the cosmic] egg
with his ankleted [feet] that enveloped the whole [earth] garden reaching in all eight directions
that day measured the world, with lightning for [his] attire, is the king
who protected the cows with the mountain as parasol
gloss: participial noun, perfective aspect, singular, masculine, third person

en: Who as cowherd grazed the cow herds, blew the flute
who as strong man tore open the horse, the sapphire-coloured one
he, staying in a lion form, with [his] nails understand
angrily tore the chest of Hiraṇya
The world is inside the unique chest of the one
with big garlands on his breast, who restrained inside
[his] great chest as a gift the earth, covered in fields
having bent the firm tusk of the angry big rutting bull elephant
By the two feet of him with the green-golden crown
that spreads many rays, of him who is the world, the aeons
the ocean, the [sun] rays expanding with bright lustre, and red fire
be filled, my heart, [and] desire [them]
gloss: participial noun, imperfective aspect, singular, masculine, third person
pronominalised noun, singular, masculine, third person

en: Vēṅkaṭam
where the rutting bull elephant out of desire sulks with [his] dark cow
runs about, fights out of anger [and] drops pearls from [his] wide, excellent
white tusks, is the mountain of him
who on an earlier day took the earth on [his] tusk
gloss: participial noun, singular, masculine, perfective aspect

en: The one who that day put Vācuki on top of the mountain [and] curled [it around]
seizing with one hand the top of [its] head, [and] churned the ocean so that
the [cosmic] egg went to the top of the waves [and] water splashed
he is the lord who stood there as a clod
gloss: participial noun, masculine singular, perfective aspect

en: O great lord who stood there receiving water, o great lord
who traversed all the worlds, o red-eyed one, you with the tulsi crown
who that day tore apart the mouth of the horse, for us
you also tore apart the mouth of hell
gloss: participial noun, perfective aspect, singular, second person

en: You, isn’t it, received water [and] measured the world with [your] foot?
You, isn’t it, stood [and] grazed the herds? You, isn’t it
tore apart the horse’s mouth, went in between the big myrobalan trees
[and] fought furiously [in the battle of] gods [and] Asuras
Going to the unapproachable Hiraṇya and destroying [him], receiving [water and]
obtaining the great earth [were yours]. For Piṉṉai’s sake, you obliterated
the strength of the bull, standing in front of [him, his] might ruined
you with the great conch that rises with spirals all around
gloss: neuter singular, perfective aspect, verbal noun
verbal noun, neuter singular, perfective aspect

en: Māl with the flashing jewel crown with a tulsi garland all around
killed the big crocodile that had grown in the pool with sapphire water
on the broad mountain into which plunges the descending waterfall
he with adorning blue [lotus] colour
gloss: participial noun, masculine singular, perfective aspect

en: It’s him who protected the cow herds with the mountain difficult [to lift]
It’s him who bent the decorative myrobalan trees. It’s him
who shows the unperturbed big city, look
he who discharged [arrows] at Ilaṅkāpuram [and] burned it
gloss: participial noun, masculine singular, perfective aspect
participial noun, masculine singular, perfective aspect
participial noun, masculine singular, perfective aspect

en: He discharged [arrows] at all seven Cadamba trees as Rāma
He discharged [arrows] at that fawn for [her with] eminent jewels. When
as soon as he had discharged [arrows at him], the king of Southern Laṅkā fell
he once went in the form of a dwarf [and], toiling, took over the earth
gloss: participial noun, perfective aspect, singular, masculine, third person
participial noun, perfective aspect, singular, masculine, third person
neuter singular, perfective aspect, verbal noun

en: Diligently worship, heart the feet of him with a cool swaying garland
as a miraculous child in the flood that had taken the goodness
of the one earth, abiding there by the banyan, on the banyan leaf of a tree
that moved forward in the ancient water, the ocean
To him whose chest a woman enjoys, there, after he, as a boar, had incurably
split the chest of the earth, after having gone between the myrobalan trees
after pushing the bull [and] kicking the cart with [his] foot
love [for him] is great in the chest of the woman
While he, wearing a big garland on [his] big mountain[-like] chest
roams about like lightning between black clouds
is the lotus, around which bees quietly hum a melody
[still] of the colour that is shown by [his] long drawn-out eyes
‘[His] colours are white, red, green, black’:
if we count thus we won’t know the form of the lord. In [her] profusion
the Lady of the tongue alone is capable of praising the goodness
the splendour of the husband of the Lady from the flower
The ankleted [feet] of the one on whose chest Śrī is joyfully sitting
appearing like lightning among the ample darkening rain clouds
[the feet] of the black one whom Garuḍa has grandly taken upon himself
in [your] perception see [them] clearly
gloss: participial noun, singular, second person, perfective aspect

en: Vēṅkaṭam, where the she-monkey that sits on the bright rock
looks at the male monkey who cares for [her and] says
‘give [me] the shining white moon,’ is the residence of him who rejoiced
on a former day, in taking the earth into [his] mind
gloss: participial noun, masculine singular, perfective aspect

en: I have understood a way of living
after having gotten to join the feet of our great lord
red-eyed Māl, the one of great sapphire colour, with Śrī who enfolds
[him] so that she lies as a garland, like a waterfall that comes down
from a high mountain [dark] as kajal
He who, successfully protecting the cows, going in between the entwined myrobalam trees
drinking from the breast of the demoness, kicking the horse cart
took a calf stick [and] threw it for the woodapple fruits is the one who once
rejoiced in putting the conch to [his] mouth in victory
gloss: participial noun, masculine singular, perfective aspect
participial noun, masculine singular, perfective aspect

en: As in all earlier times Vēṅkaṭam, the milk ocean [and] Vaikuntam
were the temples for him who took [them and] dwelled there
[so now is] Kaṭikai, with lush flowers in long groves where a wealth of bees
rises, the heavenly city for the young prince
gloss: participial noun, masculine singular, dative, imperfective aspect

en: The heavenly city Veḵkā, Vēṅkaṭam [encircled] by water with expanding waves
the earth city Vēḷukkai with big mansions, Southern Kuṭantai
interior to(?) the earth, honey-filled Tiruvaraṅkam, Southern Kōṭṭi
he received humbly, with water in his palm
gloss: participial noun, perfective aspect, singular, masculine, third person

en: Hanging matted hair and tall crown, bright axe and discus
coiling snakes and gold string appear indeed on the holy mountain
where all around waterfalls gather [and] spread
two forms for our Father, having joined as one
Lying, sitting and standing there in Kacci, in Veḵkā
is that endurance for [him who] churned to exhaustion
in order to bring forth the ambrosia there after having united
the consenting snake, mountain and ocean?
gloss: verbal noun, neuter singular, perfective aspect

en: He is the father who in the form of a lion foamed
[and] broke open the chest of Hiraṇya, so that he died
at the time of twilight, without harm to the son
he who heatedly broke off the tusk from the elephant form
gloss: participial noun, masculine singular, perfective aspect

en: When you, hotly dispelling darkness, breathed on the rays
of the cobra’s hood that resembles big sapphires shining with rays
the approaching Matu and Kaiṭavar died, [their] bellies melting
That was the ruin, thus the end, of those
In the navel of Māl, where there are blossoms heaped
there is a bright bud of a high lotus peering
at the discus in [his] hand, thinking [it] the sun
[and] at the white conch, thinking [it] the moon that shines in the sky
Vēṅkaṭam, where the peering monkey sees [its own] reflection in the water
of the mountain pool, moves on in the thought ‘another monkey’ [and]
extends [its] hand for the blackened Kaḷam fruits, is the mountain of him
who, on a former day, threw the calf for the fruits of the woodapple tree
gloss: participial noun, masculine singular, perfective aspect

en: She sings Vēṅkaṭam as ‘mountain’; she wears copious
tulsi as [a sign of] fidelity on [her] black curls; in order to bath
she enters on all the days that come the long sea where Māl lied
[his] shoulder extended so that [the wrestlers] were destroyed in wrestling
Smearing [its] mouth with ichor so that it enters [there], washing [its] feet with ichor
that falls [and] drips into the waterfall, taking with [its] trunk the blossom
that unfolds with very heady honey, the bull elephant bows
upon seeing the victorious lord of Vēṅkaṭam
Vēṅkaṭam
where the bull elephant stands [and] trumpets after having, trunk raised
so that it pierces the clouds, run at [and] killed the Yāḷi, so that it fell
roaring, [its] paw broken by the shining tusk
is the hill of him who on a former day threw the young calf
gloss: participial noun, masculine singular, perfective aspect

en: Vēṅkaṭam
where the hill women who are on the sole hill, go [their] hands with pretty
bangles moving, to the playing sweet bamboo [flute and] victoriously
make the planet set the shining moon free
is the place of the king of young princes above
Speaking of the tinkling anklets of him who stood as a dancer
who longs for pots, who dwells on north-facing Vēṅkaṭam
driving the sun chariot, yoked with seven [horses] left [and] right
is a good [action] that exists by the tongue itself
gloss: participial noun, singular, masculine, perfective aspect
imperfective aspect, verbal noun, neuter singular

en: Is it strong, the goodness
of the cowherdess who again put [him] close to her breast in
order to feed him, him who had drunk only water from the cruel breast
so that the strong demoness fell to the ground in contortions
having fed [him] poison?
gloss: participial noun, masculine singular, accusative, perfective aspect
participial noun, feminine singular, perfective aspect

en: The sacred mountain
where the angry tiger peers closely at the bright hare in the white moon
that moves up crawling to the curved mountain top
in order to closely rub [its] belly, is the height
that is fragrant of the kino tree by the cowherd’s fields
Not wanting to stand on heights, bathe in floods and stand
midst the five fires, if you truly strew blossoms [and] fold
[your] hands in worship to the one who joined desirable Veḵkā
[your] evil deeds will dwindle [and] pass away
gloss: participial noun, masculine singular, accusative, perfective aspect

en: He who, as a superior child on the good thighs of the one
with the choice difficult Vedas, the one with four faces, accurately
counted as three [plus] seven the crowns suited to the sword[-wearing] Rākṣasa
[his] foot blossoms that [we] drink in are our refuge
gloss: participial noun, masculine singular, perfective aspect

en: Refuge for us is always the one with the discus on his right. If there is refuge
[it is] the one by whose prowess the strength [and] the days of Muraṉ were curbed
Without asking ‘which way, which condition, which birth?’
recite, perceiving the Dark one as the way
If, as people with concentrated minds, they restrain the five [senses], examine
[and] destroy [them], there will be destruction of all the seven births
constantly [concentrated] on the one whose chest has rows of garlands
with the complexion of the swelling flood, with dark, fragrant tulsi full of scent
The red feet of him on the serpent bed, with the sharpened white discus
that shines victoriously when the combined twice five hundred arms of Bāṇa
are cut all together, who had stood up against [him] on a chariot with jewels in rows
[my] heart strains to get close [to them]
gloss: pronominalised noun, singular, masculine, third person

en: Even though he is difficult to think about by the heart, take a stand
my heart, speak [anyway]. When one thinks [about it], what [is the point]
of perception that remains without contemplating our great Lord
who stands unmoved in the heart?
gloss: pronominalised noun, concessive, conditional, masculine singular
participial noun, neuter singular, imperfective aspect

en: When perceiving he is difficult to perceive. Even when he has entered [our] heart
[and] connected [with us] his nature is difficult to see. Where may we now
see [him] closely, the king with cool tulsi in which bees hum
closing in on the pollen so that they are close to the clusters?
Even though now they say that he is the Dark one
even though now he is difficult to see, he now [already]
is inside [my] heart, he with the green-golden anklets
who by [his] guile took the earth [and] crossed the sky
gloss: concessive, conditional, imperfective aspect, honorific, third person
pronominalised noun, concessive, conditional, masculine singular

en: Even though, as he is [already] in the heart, they search [and] perceive
the inner meaning of the four Vedas that is him, who are those
who have seen the cunning one with large eyes, lush lotuses
who [always] is [there]? They are those that rejoice in poetry
gloss: concessive, conditional, imperfective aspect, honorific, third person
pronominalised noun, singular, masculine, accusative, third person
participial noun, honorific, third person, perfective aspect

en: They who fold [their] hands [before] poets, who go to the ankleted [feet] to [their] eyes’ fill
[and] who frequent Veda experts who have ears [to hear] the people of the earth
while they praise [and] recite, it will flourish, the beauty
of him who for Piṉṉai’s sake destroyed the life of the bull
gloss: participial noun, honorific, third person, perfective aspect
participial noun, masculine singular, perfective aspect

en: Like graceful water clouds that appear, gracefully
raising the banner of lightning, speedily taking up work
thundering, like of the colour of tall Māl
the sky shows itself, mingled with rain clouds
O Kaṇṇaṉ, on whom the jewel diffusely twinkles, your body
in bloom shows itself as an emerald. The sky at dusk is
what shows the king with cool tulsi, where bees hum
on the garland strings glittering with beauty
Without being in doubt that that is good [and] this is evil
worship the [feet with] golden anklets that rest common [to all]
[the feet] of him with honey-rich cool tulsi on his chest
All former deeds will end [and] dissolve
Vēṅkaṭam
where the bamboo, that rises after having been cut, when the hill people
at an advanced time had sown fresh millet into the furrows ploughed
in lying down by the wild boars, grows tall [and] opens up to the sky
is the slope of him who on a former day put the sweet flute to [his] mouth
gloss: participial noun, singular, masculine, third person, perfective aspect

en: When [his] red feet that were rinsed in the heavenly river go [to the top of the world] egg
so that [his] foot rings and tight anklets sound in movement
[and his] sole arms encompass all the eight directions, which place did it not reach
the earth that was measured by Māl with lush tulsi?
Being insatiable after eating the earth and drinking from the breast of the demoness
he, whom the cowherdess, in anger because he swallowed the butter
bound with a knotted rope, remained bound
the son with an unsatiable stomach
gloss: participial noun, singular, masculine, perfective aspect

en: The trickster with a dark body who is not the son of anyone
became a son. The one who subdued the arms of Bāṇa, who put into prison
the beloved son of the son of him, make yourself full
of the ankleted [feet of him], my heart, think!
gloss: pronominalised noun, dative, honorific, third person
participial noun, masculine singular, perfective aspect

en: Who are those in the world who understand [him] by thought? Tirumāl
who became tall, him who, keeping the whole world inside [himself], as a child
on the banyan [leaf] in the roaring, roiling sea, slept softly
put [him] directly inside [yourself], o heart
gloss: participial noun, masculine singular, accusative, perfective aspect

en: Raising the lamp that directly takes up the light called perception
holding [it and] seeking him out, I caught [him] in the net. Softly
unfailingly entering into my heart, the Dark one
stands, sits [and] lies [there]
The holy feet of Tirumāl, who as a lion tore up the chest of Hiraṇya
who had scorned [him], so that it got shredded [and] scattered
everywhere at the time that twilight entered [and] glowed
[these feet] laude [and] praise, my heart
Because the celestials, as those whose mouths praise [him], lower
[their] jewelled crowns [and] bow [to them], they are scarred
the blossoms that are the lotus feet of the husband
of the girl on the lotus blossom with a lustrous stalk
The one with the navel where is borne the blossom, the Cunning one with dark body
where is borne the Blossom in whom is beauty, can he, [even]
for a moment, be regarded by these people: the one with the colour
borne by the blossom, the one from the great blossom, [or] the one with the long, matted hair?

en: As the mountains embraced by snow, as the vast sky and as wind
he appears fully luminous all around(?)
the one who protects us from getting near hell embraced by Yama
the one who by touch tore open the mouth of the horse

en: The victorious one whose eight weapons, which he grasps, are unvanquished
the one with eight arms [and] hands, the one with the discus that he threw
at that time, aiming at the murderous crocodile when it slept in the pond
at [his] feet [there is] refuge for us
Refuge for us [is] always Śrī on the honey-filled flower
with large eyes, lush lotuses, that twinkle [like] lightning dwelling
in the rain-filled cloud, who is embraced by him with the mountain chest
alive with a garland of cool tulsi, the one with the discus
